title: 30년간 결혼 반토막, 외국인과 혼인 54%↑...출생아는 3분의 1로 | 연합뉴스
content:
South Korea’s marriage and birth statistics over the last three decades show a sharp decline in overall marriages and births, a rise in foreign‑partner marriages, and a shift toward later first marriages and lower fertility.  The total number of marriages peaked in 1996 at 434,900 and fell to 191,700 in 2022, a 44.2 % drop from 30 years earlier.  In 2023 the figure rose slightly to 193,700 and in 2024 to 222,400, yet it remains far below the 1995 level.  Foreign‑partner marriages increased from 13,500 in 1995 to 28,000 in 2024, a 53.9 % rise, and now account for 9.3 % of all marriages—roughly one in ten.  Marriages between Korean men and foreign women grew 50.7 % (from 14,000 to 15,600), while those between Korean women and foreign men rose 64.2 % (from 3,100 to 5,000).  The average age at first marriage rose from 28.4 years for men and 25.3 years for women in 1995 to 33.9 years for men and 31.6 years for women in 2024, an increase of 5.5 years for men and 6.2 years for women.

Births fell dramatically from 715,000 in 1995 to 238,000 in 2023, a 66.7 % decline, and the total fertility rate dropped from 1.63 children per woman in 1995 to 0.75 in 2024, a 54.2 % reduction.  Age‑specific birth rates show that women aged 25–29 had 20.7 births per 1,000 women in 2024, while those aged 30–34 and 35–39 had 70.4 and 46.0, respectively—higher than in 1995.  Among married women, the birth rate per 1,000 married women was 203.5 (25–29), 171.5 (30–34) and 69.1 (35–39) in 2024, indicating that births are concentrating among married couples.

The average age at first birth rose from 27.9 years in 1995 to 33.7 years in 2024, a 5.8‑year increase, while the average age at second birth climbed from 31.1 to 36.1 years.  The proportion of first‑born children fell from 48.4 % in 1995 to 61.3 % in 2024, a 13‑percentage‑point rise, because the decline in second and third births (75.4 % and 73.5 % respectively) was steeper.  The share of births outside marriage grew from 1.2 % to 5.8 %, and multiple‑births increased from 1.3 % to 5.7 %.

A statistician noted, '20대 후반과 30대 초반의 유배우 출산율이 2015년 정점을 보인 후 하락했다가 2022년부터 상승하고 있다' and added that "결혼한 사람 가운데서는 출산이 늘고 있다는 의미".

These data illustrate a trend toward later marriage and childbearing, a decline in overall fertility, and a growing role of multicultural marriages in South Korea’s demographic landscape.

title: Fertility growth led by rebound in second-child births
content: According to Statistics Korea's August 27 release, the number of births in South Korea rose to 238,300 last year, up 3.6 % (8,300) from 230,000 in 2024. The total fertility rate increased to 0.75, up 0.03 from 0.72. Second‑child births reached 75,900, up 2.0 % (1,500) after falling to 74,400 in 2023. Third‑child births fell 5.8 % to 16,200. Regional fertility rates were highest in South Jeolla and Sejong (1.03) and lowest in Seoul (0.58). The average age of parents at first birth was 35.4 years for fathers and 33.1 years for mothers. In June, 19,953 babies were born, a 9.4 % increase (1,709) over June 2024, the largest growth rate for June since 1981. The cumulative first‑half births reached 126,001, up 8,721 (7.4 %) from the same period last year, with first‑half and second‑quarter growth rates of 7.4 % and 7.3 % respectively – record highs. A Statistics Korea official said, 'The recent expansion of multi‑child benefits from three children to two appears to have had a positive effect on parents considering having a second child,' and added, 'The rise in marriages since the first quarter of last year, an increase in the population of women in their 30s, and a shift toward more positive perceptions of childbirth have all contributed to the increase in fertility.'

title: '역대 최고' 찍은 출생아 증가율...합계출산율 0.8명 달성 '청신호'
content: In the first half of 2025, South Korea recorded a 7.4 % rise in live births, reaching 126,001 compared with 117,280 in the same period of 2024, the highest growth rate since 1981.  Regional data show increases in Seoul (9.2 %), Incheon (12.1 %), Chungcheong North (11.6 %) and Daegu (10.9 %).  June’s birth count of 19,953 was up 9.4 % from June 2024, and July‑December 2024 has shown a 12‑month streak of growth.  The second‑quarter total fertility rate (TFR) rose to 0.76, a 0.05‑point increase over the previous year.  Experts note that the TFR could reach 0.8, citing a surge in births among women aged 30‑34 (143,072) and a projected 300,000+ births this year.  Professor Jeong Young‑soo of Hanyang University said, '올해 0.8명 달성은 어렵지 않아 보인다' and added that the post‑COVID concentration of marriages and births is driving the rise.  Professor Lee Sang‑ryum of Seoul National University’s Population Policy Research Center remarked, '올해는 반등하는 추세로 합계출산율이 0.8명 수준을 넘을 것 같다' and warned that birth growth may stall if housing, employment and childcare support do not improve.  Professor Lee Seung‑yoon of Chung‑Ang University cautioned, '출산율 증가는 긍정적인 신호지만 낙관하기는 이르다' and called for labor‑time reduction and expanded parental leave.  The article stresses that policy backing—such as stable housing prices and expanded birth support—is essential to sustain the current upward trend.

title: Number of births rise for 13th consecutive month
content: Statistics Korea released data showing that the number of births in South Korea rose for the 13th consecutive month in July 2025. A total of 21,803 babies were born, an increase of 1,223 or 5.9 percent from July 2024 (Statistics Korea). This is the highest July figure since 2021, when 22,364 births were recorded, but it remains the fourth‑lowest July count since 1981, with the lowest July figure of 19,085 births recorded in 2023. From January to July 2025, 147,804 births were registered, a 7.2 percent rise over the same period in 2024, marking the first cumulative increase in ten years and the largest year‑on‑year growth since records began (Statistics Korea). The rise is attributed to more marriages, government child‑birth support policies, and a higher number of women in their early 30s. The total fertility rate in July was 0.80, up 0.04 from July 2024 (Statistics Korea). Births increased in 13 of 17 cities and provinces, including Seoul and Busan, while falling in four, such as Gwangju and Sejong. First‑born children accounted for 61.9 percent of births, up 1.6 percentage points, whereas second‑born and third‑born or later shares fell to 31.4 percent and 6.7 percent, respectively. Marriages rose to 20,394 in July, an increase of 1,583 or 8.4 percent year‑over‑year, the highest July figure in nine years since 21,154 marriages were recorded in July 2016 (Statistics Korea). Marriages have been rising for 16 consecutive months since April 2024. Deaths totaled 27,979, down 200 or 0.7 percent from the previous year, and divorces fell to 7,826, down 113 or 1.4 percent, continuing a seven‑month decline. Despite the birth increase, deaths still outpaced births, resulting in a natural population decline of 6,175 people in July (Statistics Korea).

title: 女초혼 연령 30년 전보다 6.2세 많아졌다...20대母 출산율 '뚝'
content:
The 2025 Statistics Korea report shows that the average age at first marriage has risen sharply over the past 30 years. Women’s average first‑marriage age increased from 25.4 to 31.6 years (a rise of 6.2 years), while men’s age rose from 28.4 to 33.9 years (5.5 years). The gap between genders narrowed from 3.0 to 2.3 years. Total marriages peaked in 1996 at 435,000 and fell to 192,000 in 2022, but have risen again since 2023. The joint marriage rate per 1,000 people fell from 8.7 to 4.4, a drop of 4.3. Remarriage ages are 51.6 years for men and 41.7 years for women, up 11.2 and 6.1 years respectively, with remarriage proportions at 14.1 % (men) and 15.4 % (women). Foreign‑partner marriages have increased, with the share of foreign spouses rising from 3.4 % in 1995 to 9.3 % in 2024.

Birth statistics mirror the marriage trend. Total births fell from 715,000 in 1995 to a low of 230,000 in 2023, then rebounded to 238,000 in 2024. The joint birth rate per 1,000 people dropped from 15.7 to 4.7, a decline of 11.0. The total fertility rate fell from 1.63 to 0.75, a drop of 0.89. Age‑specific fertility shifted: births in women’s 20s declined, while those in the 30s and early 40s increased. The average maternal age rose to 33.7 years (up 5.8) and paternal age to 36.1 years (up 5.0). High‑age mothers (35+) accounted for 35.9 % of births in 2024, up from 4.8 % in 1995.

Twin and higher‑order births grew from 1.3 % to 5.7 % of all births, and non‑marital births increased from 1.2 % to 5.8 %. The proportion of first‑born children conceived within two years of marriage fell from 83.0 % in 1995 to 52.6 % in 2024.

Quotes from the report: '평균초혼연령은 여자의 경우 지속적으로 상승했고 남자는 2020년과 2024년을 제외하고 상승했다' and '출생아 수는 1995년 71만5000명에서 감소 추세를 보이다가 2023년 23만명으로 최저를 기록한 후 지난해 23만8000명으로 오랜만에 반등했다'.

title: 2분기 합계출산율 0.76명...증가율 역대 최대
content: According to Statistics Korea’s June 2025 population‑trend report, the second‑quarter total fertility rate rose to 0.76 children per woman, an increase of 0.05 from the same period last year.  The number of births in the second quarter reached 69,979, up 4,157 (7.3 %) compared with the previous year, marking the largest quarterly growth rate since 1981 and the largest scale since the second quarter of 2021.  In June alone, 19,953 babies were born, a 9.4 % rise (1,709 more) over June 2024.  June births had been declining since 2015, but after a decade of decline the trend reversed, with monthly births increasing for 12 consecutive months since July 2024.  The growth is partly attributed to the larger population in the 30‑34 age group, the so‑called second baby‑boom generation.  Park Hyun‑jeong, head of the population‑trend division, explained that the rise in marriage numbers and the larger main birth‑age cohort were major drivers, adding that changing attitudes toward marriage and childbirth and related policies also contributed.  Marriage figures continued to climb: June marriages numbered 18,487, a 9.1 % increase year‑on‑year, and the second‑quarter total reached 59,169, up 5.8 %.  June divorces fell to 6,777 (‑6 %), while deaths rose to 27,270 (‑1.5 %).  The natural population increase—births minus deaths—declined by 7,317.  Park Hyun‑jeong said, '혼인 건수와 주 출산 연령 규모가 증가한 영향이 크다' and '결혼·출산에 대한 인식 변화와 정책적인 부분도 영향을 미친 거로 보인다'.

title: S. Korea marriages halved, births down 2/3, 30-year report shows
content:
South Korea’s marriage and birth rates have fallen sharply over the past 30 years. The crude marriage rate dropped from 8.7 per 1,000 people in 1995 to 4.4 in 2024, and total marriages peaked at 434,900 in 1996 before falling to 191,700 in 2022; 2024’s 222,400 marriages are still 44 % below the 1995 level. Average marriage age rose from 28.4 to 33.9 for men and from 25.3 to 31.6 for women, pushing most unions into the 30s and 40s. Subsequent marriages increased to 14.1 % of men and 15.4 % of women in 2024. International marriages grew from 13,500 (3.4 %) in 1995 to 20,800 (9.3 %) in 2024, a 51 % rise for Korean men with foreign women and a 64 % rise for Korean women with foreign men.

Births have declined even more sharply: 715,000 in 1995 versus 238,000 in 2024, a 67 % drop. The total fertility rate fell from 1.63 to 0.75, and the crude birth rate fell from 15.7 to 4.7 per 1,000 people. Mothers’ average age at birth rose from 27.9 to 33.7 years, and births to women 35 or older jumped from 4.8 % to 35.9 %. Firstborns fell 58 % (from 345,800 to 146,100), second births 75 % and third births 74 %. The average gap between marriage and first childbirth increased from 1.5 to 2.5 years. Children born outside marriage rose from 1.2 % to 5.8 %, and multiple births increased from 1.3 % to 5.7 %. A Statistics Korea official noted that fertility rates among married women in their late 20s and early 30s peaked in 2015, declined, and have been rising again since 2022. 'This means that among those who do marry, births are increasing,' the official explained. The steepest birth declines occurred in South Gyeongsang (‑80 %), Busan (‑75 %) and North Jeolla (‑75 %). In contrast, the Seoul metropolitan area accounted for more than half of all births in 2024, led by Gyeonggi Province (28 %), Seoul (19 %) and Incheon (6 %).

title: 평균 출산연령 33.7세...혼외 출생아 1만3800명 역대 최대
content: Statistics Korea’s 2024 birth statistics show that the average age of mothers at childbirth rose to 33.7 years, up 0.1 year from the previous year. The share of children born outside marriage reached 5.8 %, the highest level on record, with 13,800 unmarried births reported. Total births for 2023 were 238,300, a 3.6 % increase (8,300 more) compared with 2022 – the first rise in nine years. First‑born children numbered 7,800 (5.6 % of all births) and second‑born children 1,500 (2.0 %), while births of third or higher order fell by 1,000 (‑5.8 %). Twin and higher‑order births accounted for 5.7 % (13,500 cases), a 0.2‑point rise, and mothers who delivered twins were on average 35.3 years old, 1.7 years older than mothers of singletons. The average number of children a woman is expected to give birth to over her lifetime increased to 0.75, a 0.03‑point rise from 2023, halting a nine‑year decline. Fathers’ average age was 36.1 years. Regional fertility rates varied, with Jeollanam‑do and Sejong at 1.03 children per woman – the highest – and Seoul and Busan at 0.58 and 0.68 respectively, none approaching the replacement fertility level of 2.1. Park Hyun‑jeong, head of population trends, noted that the shift in the perception that "marriage is required to have children" has had a major impact, adding that the proportion of respondents who answered positively to the question "You can have children without marrying" rose from 21.5 % in 2008 to 37.2 % in 2024.

title: 6월 출생아 2만명 육박, 9.4% 증가...6월 기준 역대 최대 증가율 - 머니투데이
content: According to Statistics Korea’s 27 August 2025 release of the ‘June 2025 Population Trend’, the number of births in June 2025 was 19,953, a rise of 1,709 (9.4 %) from the same month in 2024, marking the highest growth rate since the 1981 statistical compilation. The June birth figure is the largest since 2 June 2021, when 21,504 babies were born. In the first half of 2025, 126,001 births were recorded, a 7.4 % increase over the first half of 2024. The second‑quarter birth total of 69,979 was 4,157 (7.3 %) higher than the previous year’s figure, the largest quarterly increase since the second quarter of 2011. The June total fertility rate, the expected number of children a woman in child‑bearing age would have over her lifetime, was 0.76, up 0.06 from the previous year, with the most pronounced rise among women in their 30s. The age‑specific fertility rate for 30‑year‑olds rose from 0.82 in January to 0.76 in June. The crude birth rate per 1,000 population was 4.8, up 0.4 from the previous year. Birth growth is attributed to a rise in marriages and an increase in the 30‑year‑old female population, alongside a more positive public perception of marriage and child‑bearing. Marriages in June 2025 numbered 18,487, a 9.1 % increase over June 2024 and the highest monthly figure since 2018. The second‑quarter marriage total of 59,169 was 5.8 % higher than the previous year, continuing a six‑quarter streak of growth. Divorce figures fell: June divorces were 6,777, a 6.0 % decline from June 2024, and the second‑quarter total of 21,489 was 5.9 % lower. Natural population decline remains a concern; June deaths were 27,270, a 1.5 % rise, and the June natural decline (births minus deaths) was 7,317. The cumulative natural decline for the first half of 2025 reached 59,460, and South Korea has experienced 68 consecutive months of natural decline since November 2019.

title: 출산율 0.8명 눈앞...출산 연령 평균 33.7세·혼외 비중 '역대 최고' (종합)
content:
The Financial News report shows that South Korea’s birth rate is rebounding after nine years of decline, with the annual birth rate expected to approach 0.8 children per woman this year.  According to Statistics Korea’s 2024 birth statistics, the total number of births last year was 238,300, a 3.6 % increase from the previous year.  The total fertility rate rose modestly from 0.72 to 0.75, the highest in nine years since 2015.  In June 2024, the number of births was 19,953, up 9.4 % from June 2023, and the July‑to‑December period has shown a 12‑month consecutive rise, the highest growth rate recorded by Statistics Korea for June.  The first‑half cumulative births reached 126,001, a 7.4 % increase over the same period last year, the largest first‑half growth rate on record.

The report cites Statistics Korea’s head of population trends, Park Hyun‑jeong, who explained that "혼인 증가, 30대 여성 인구 확대, 출산에 대한 인식 변화 등이 복합적으로 영향을 미쳤다" (increased marriages, a larger population of women in their 30s, and changing attitudes toward childbirth).  The Korea Future Population Research Institute’s director, Lee In‑sil, added that "합계출산율 0.8명 진입은 충분히 가능하다" and that the rise reflects an increase in women of child‑bearing age and behavioral changes among women who previously intended to give birth.

Despite the rebound, the structure of births remains fragile.  First‑born children accounted for 61.3 % of all births last year, up 5.6 % from the previous year, while second‑born births increased by only 2.0 % and births of three or more children fell 5.8 %.  The average age of mothers at birth is 33.7 years, with 35.9 % of mothers aged 35 years or older, meaning roughly one in three mothers is a "late‑maternal" mother.  The average age for mothers of multiples is 35.3 years, 1.7 years older than single‑birth mothers.

Unmarried births also surged, reaching 13,800 last year, 5.8 % of all births— the first time the share has exceeded 5 %.  Lee In‑sil warned that if the government treats the population issue as a "future task" rather than a crisis, the temporary rebound could fade.  He urged that the issue be elevated to a national policy led by the president, calling the current moment a "golden time" to convert the birth‑rate rebound into a long‑term growth momentum.

The article presents these facts without editorializing, offering a clear, data‑driven overview of the current demographic situation in South Korea.
